chunks: Each of the two (Talha and Zubayr) desires the Caliphate for himself, and directs it towards himself against his companion,
They do not employ any connection for getting access to Allah, nor proceed towards Him through any means.
Each of the two bears malice against the other; shortly his veil over it will be uncovered!
By Allah, if they achieve what they aim at, one of them will kill the other, and one will finish the other,
The rebellious party has stood up. Where are the seekers of virtue?
The paths have already been determined and they have been given the news,
For every misguidance there is a cause, and for every break of pledge there is a misrepresentation.
By Allah, I shall not be like him who listens to the voice of mourning, hears the man who brings news of death and also visits the mourner, yet does not take lesson!

key_terms.الْفِئَةُ الْبَاغِيَةُ: The rebellious party (referring to Talha, Zubayr, and their followers)
key_terms.الْمُحْتَسِبُونَ: Seekers of virtue / those who count good deeds
key_terms.نَاكِثٍ: One who breaks a pledge (specifically referring to the breakers of the peace treaty with Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali predict about the rivalry between Talha and Zubayr?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes the rivalry between Talha and Zubayr as a mutual, unanchored ambition where each sought the Caliphate while harboring hidden resentment, predicting that their success would lead to immediate mutual destruction. He contextualizes this within the broader phenomenon of the 'rebellious faction' (al-Fat al-Baghiya), noting that every deviation has its pretext and every oath-breaker its justification, urging believers to actively learn from these events rather than remaining passive observers.
